text: It does not. Even the lowest sound we can hear, twenty hertz, squeezes each layer twenty times a second. At a thousand hertz, a compression lasts only half a millisecond. And air is a very poor conductor of heat. So practically no heat leaves a compression, or enters a rarefaction. The changes are not isothermal. They are adiabatic.
